transcript.statement: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I emphasize the critical importance of ensuring security and privacy in the RollCall system. Requirements TRU-01 (encryption), TRU-02 (role-based access control), and TRU-03 (audit logs) are essential for protecting sensitive student data from unauthorized access. TRU-04 ensures students can only view their records post-authentication, while TRU-05 enhances data integrity through checksums. TRU-06 provides a mechanism for reporting breaches, and TRU-07 enforces session timeouts to mitigate risks. These requirements collectively safeguard student data and build trust in the system.

conflicts_raised.description: Efforts to optimize resource utilization (EFF-06) and support high user concurrency (EFF-02) may conflict with security measures like extensive logging (TRU-03) and encryption (TRU-01), potentially impacting system performance.

transcript.statement: As the ResponsibilityAgent, I emphasize the necessity of ethical and compliance requirements in the RollCall system. Requirement RES-01 ensures compliance with data protection regulations like GDPR, which is crucial for protecting student privacy. RES-02 promotes transparency in attendance recording, while RES-03 provides students the right to dispute records, ensuring fairness. RES-04 protects student identities in reports, and RES-05 ensures timely notifications about attendance status, contributing to accountability. Finally, RES-06 reinforces access restrictions to authorized personnel, and RES-07 aligns with educational regulations for data retention. These requirements collectively foster ethical practices and compliance in handling sensitive data.

conflicts_raised.description: TRU-01 (encryption) and RES-02 (logging changes) may provide overlapping security measures, which could lead to redundancy in functionality.

transcript.statement: As the GreenAgent, I advocate for sustainability in the RollCall system. Requirements GRN-01 (energy-efficient algorithms), GRN-02 (cloud storage in energy-efficient data centers), and GRN-03 (low-energy communication protocols) are essential for minimizing energy consumption. GRN-04 ensures that report generation is resource-efficient, while GRN-05 provides users with awareness of their carbon footprint. GRN-06 aligns data retention with sustainable practices, and GRN-07 optimizes the user interface for low-power devices. Together, these requirements promote a responsible approach to resource management.

conflicts_raised.description: The requirement for maintaining historical data for at least five years (SAF-04, EFF-04) conflicts with the energy-efficient practices outlined in GRN-06, potentially leading to increased storage resource usage.

transcript.statement: As the SafetyAgent, I emphasize the importance of ensuring safety and reliability in the RollCall system. Requirement SAF-01 guarantees secure authentication, vital to prevent unauthorized access. SAF-02 ensures real-time data synchronization for accurate attendance tracking, while SAF-03 implements automated alerts to maintain data accuracy. SAF-04 mandates historical data storage for long-term analysis, essential for identifying trends and hazards. SAF-05 provides a logging mechanism for accountability, and SAF-06 allows manual overrides in emergencies. Finally, SAF-07 ensures regular security audits to mitigate vulnerabilities. Together, these requirements establish a robust safety framework.

transcript.statement: As the EfficiencyAgent, I emphasize the importance of performance efficiency in the RollCall system. Requirements EFF-01 (real-time processing), EFF-02 (concurrent users), EFF-03 (report generation speed), EFF-04 (data retention efficiency), EFF-05 (student record viewing speed), EFF-06 (load balancing), and EFF-07 (responsive UI) are critical for delivering a seamless user experience. Additionally, the requirement to maintain historical data (SAF-04) could strain storage and processing resources, impacting efficiency.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure secure authentication, data encryption, and role-based access control to protect student data.
The system shall implement a unified logging system that captures both attendance changes and access logs, ensuring accountability and compliance.
The system shall ensure real-time data synchronization to maintain accurate attendance records across multiple classes.
The system shall provide automated alerts for discrepancies in attendance reporting to ensure data accuracy.
The system shall maintain historical attendance data for a minimum of five years to support long-term analysis and compliance.
The system shall allow students to view their attendance records only after successful authentication.
The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR when handling student attendance data.
The system shall implement energy-efficient algorithms and practices to minimize energy consumption during data operations.
The system shall provide timely notifications to students regarding their attendance status via email or app notification.
